groups.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

parts.context: A tutor discusses a water-saving experiment in student houses with two students.

transcript.text: Hello Emma, hello Raj. Please tell me about your water-saving experiment in the student houses.
transcript.speaker: MR GREEN

transcript.text: Our houses were all in the same street, so they have similar plumbing, which makes the comparison fairer.
transcript.speaker: EMMA

transcript.text: Good. That should go in your methods section.
transcript.speaker: MR GREEN

transcript.text: We chose six houses and asked the students to record how much water they used every day for a month.
transcript.speaker: EMMA

transcript.text: In the second month, we gave them a small timer for the shower. It makes a noise after five minutes.
transcript.speaker: RAJ

transcript.text: Did it work?
transcript.speaker: MR GREEN

transcript.text: Yes. The average use fell by twenty percent, from about two hundred litres to one hundred and sixty per person per day.
transcript.speaker: EMMA

transcript.text: That's a significant difference. Was it the same in every house?
transcript.speaker: MR GREEN

transcript.text: Not exactly. Some houses saved more than others, depending on how many people lived there.
transcript.speaker: EMMA

transcript.text: The students said the timer was annoying at first, but after a week they got used to it.
transcript.speaker: RAJ

transcript.text: Were there any problems with the measurements?
transcript.speaker: MR GREEN

transcript.text: One house had a broken meter, so we had to remove their results from the data.
transcript.speaker: EMMA

transcript.text: That's a pity, but it's good that you noticed the problem and dealt with it honestly.
transcript.speaker: MR GREEN

transcript.text: Yes, we checked all the meters twice, just to be safe.
transcript.speaker: RAJ

transcript.text: What do you think is the main reason people waste water?
transcript.speaker: MR GREEN

transcript.text: They simply don't notice. Most people have no idea how much a shower uses.
transcript.speaker: RAJ

transcript.text: Our interviews showed the same thing. People thought their showers were short, but they were actually quite long.
transcript.speaker: EMMA

transcript.text: That is a classic result. People rarely judge their own habits accurately.
transcript.speaker: MR GREEN

transcript.text: So what would you recommend to the university?
transcript.speaker: MR GREEN

transcript.text: We suggest installing timers in all halls of residence, because they cost only three pounds each.
transcript.speaker: EMMA

transcript.text: Compared with the cost of water bills, it's a very small investment, so the university should accept it easily.
transcript.speaker: RAJ

transcript.text: Present the figures clearly, though. Decision makers like simple numbers.
transcript.speaker: MR GREEN

transcript.text: Would students accept that?
transcript.speaker: MR GREEN

transcript.text: Probably, if we explain the reason. We could put a short message on the bathroom doors.
transcript.speaker: RAJ

transcript.text: We could also ask the student union to support the idea.
transcript.speaker: EMMA

transcript.text: That would be wise. They have a lot of influence with students.
transcript.speaker: MR GREEN

transcript.text: Good. When can you give me the final report?
transcript.speaker: MR GREEN

transcript.text: Next month would be easier, but I think we can finish in two weeks, on Friday the ninth.
transcript.speaker: EMMA

transcript.text: Fine. And will you present it to the Student Council?
transcript.speaker: MR GREEN

transcript.text: Yes, the Council meets on the first Tuesday of each month, so we'll go in March.
transcript.speaker: RAJ

transcript.text: I'll look forward to it. It's a practical project, and I think it could really make a difference.
transcript.speaker: MR GREEN

transcript.text: Thank you, Mr Green. We're quite proud of it.
transcript.speaker: EMMA
